assertion.statement: For the actual strongly represented limit test, its representative tests satisfy the exact unit and vertical-character identities globally on an ultrafilter-large set of indices.
assertion.objects: Fixed nilmanifold/metric and standard vertical character, represented test functions, all quotient points and all top-group elements.
assertion.hypotheses: The unit and equivariance identities already hold at every limit point and limit top-group element. The test has representatives with the stated standard Lipschitz bound.
assertion.quantifiers: All standard points and top-group elements simultaneously at each retained representative index; the premise quantifies over the entire ultraproduct domains.
assertion.parameter_range: One fixed geometry and character, with bounded representative test norms.
assertion.uniformity: One ultrafilter-large set of good indices supports both global identities; geometry and bounds remain fixed.
assertion.constants: No new effective constant. The existing representative Lipschitz bound is retained.
assertion.normalizations: Exact equality in the ultraproduct. A violating point or pair is chosen at each bad index; its ultralimit contradicts the all-limit premise.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Standard-point-only equivariance would not suffice. This step does not construct the strong input or prescribe its symbol.
assertion.limit_order: Start from represented strong data; if bad indices formed an ultrafilter-large set choose violations, apply A3 evaluation and A2 equality, obtain contradiction, then discard bad indices before the local formulas.

publication.authors: Ben Green, Terence Tao and Tamar Ziegler

available_assertion.statement: Ultralimit objects are equivalent when their representatives agree on an ultrafilter-large set; a limit function evaluates by f(lim x_n)=lim f_n(x_n).
available_assertion.objects: Sequences of standard objects, spaces and functions, their ultraproducts, and equality of their classes.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The functions and points are represented on the stated domains for ultrafilter-almost all indices.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every represented internal function and every represented point of its ultraproduct domain.
available_assertion.parameter_range: The fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter framework of Appendix A.
available_assertion.uniformity: The evaluation rule holds at all limit points, including nonstandard ones; it does not upgrade a standard-point-only identity.
available_assertion.constants: No analytic estimate is part of this rule.
available_assertion.normalizations: Equality is exact ultrafilter equality, not equality up to an infinitesimal or standard part.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: External functions need not have representatives. The rule alone supplies neither global equivariance nor a bounded-complexity family.
available_assertion.limit_order: Choose representatives of the internal objects, then evaluate and compare their equivalence classes.
